raw_response:
*Speaking as the farmer, thinking through my season:*

---

Alright, so it's mid-April now. My wheat is at jointing — the stems are starting to shoot up — and I need to decide about topdressing before heading. The sweet potato seedlings are ready to go into the ground. Stevia is already pushing up from the roots, second year for most of it. Maize I don't touch until June when the wheat comes off.

Let me think through each one.

**Wheat — 30 mu:**
I planted back in October, put down compound fertilizer as base, maybe 50 kg per mu of the diammonium plus some urea. Now at jointing I need to topdress. My neighbor Lao Chen put down 10 kg urea per mu last year at this stage and his wheat looked good at harvest, better than mine the year before when I was stingy with it. This year I'll do the same — 10 kg urea per mu now. That's about 4.6 kg pure N, on top of roughly 12-13 kg from the base. Total comes to maybe 17-18 kg N across the season. I'll irrigate once now to push the topdress in, then again at heading if it stays dry. Water costs money — my well meter runs about 0.8 yuan per cubic meter — so I try not to irrigate more than I have to.

I'm expecting around 450 kg per mu. Last year I got 430, neighbors say 470 is typical for good years. The winter wasn't too cold so I think we're okay.

**Summer Maize — same 30 mu, after wheat harvest:**
The wheat should come off by June 10th or so. I'll hire a combine for harvest — costs about 60 yuan per mu but saves three days of labor. Right after, I rent a no-till planter to get the maize in fast. No time to plow. I tried plowing the gap year before last and the maize got in five days late — that shows at harvest in September when you run out of growing days.

Maize I do base fertilizer at planting — compound again — and then I'll top-dress at the big bell stage, maybe late July. I use about 15-16 kg N total per mu for maize. Usually one bag of compound base plus two top-dresses of urea. If August is dry I'll irrigate once.

I expect 480-500 kg per mu. Market price for maize is low lately, barely above 1 yuan per jin, but I can't not grow it — the land has to have something on it after wheat, and I don't have a better option for 30 mu in summer.

**Sweet potato — 16 mu:**
This I plant this week or next. I buy slips from the village nursery, about 200 yuan per mu for slips. I ridge the beds by hand and hire two people for two days to help transplant — my wife and I can't do 16 mu alone fast enough. Sweet potato doesn't need as much nitrogen as wheat or maize, but it needs potassium to size up the roots. I apply a base of compound fertilizer with higher K, maybe 6-7 kg N per mu and 12 kg K. One or two irrigations in July-August when it's hot and dry.

Harvest is October. Yields around 1,500-1,800 kg per mu if the summer is decent. Some I sell fresh to the collector who comes to the village, some my family uses and I feed some to the pigs. Price swings a lot year to year though — bad years I get 0.3 yuan per jin, good years maybe 0.6.

**Stevia — 20 mu:**
This is my third year of stevia on most of this land. It comes back from the roots every spring so no replanting. I top-dressed a bit of compound fertilizer in March already to push early growth. First cut will be around late May or early June, just before wheat harvest gets busy — I hire four people for two days to cut and dry it. Second cut in September after the maize is harvested.

Stevia doesn't need much — maybe 10 kg N per mu across the year, spread out before each cut. One irrigation in May if spring is dry. The leaf price has been decent, around 4-5 yuan per jin dry. Last year I got about 220 kg dry leaf per mu. The processing company in town buys it all, so I'm not worried about selling it. This is my most profitable land right now, honestly.

**Budget check:**
I figure roughly 60,000-70,000 yuan for all inputs this season — fertilizer for everything, pesticides (herbicide for maize mainly, some fungicide for wheat near heading), seeds, slips, hired machinery and labor. That's tight but manageable. I try to keep 10,000-15,000 in reserve in case something breaks or prices crash.
